title: Belgium's Budget Crisis Tests the Limits of Austerity Politics in Europe · 21 Oct
keywords: Belgium, fiscal deficit, public debt, austerity, Bart De Wever, European Commission, budget crisis, strikes, protests, EU fiscal rules, coalition politics, social protection, inflation, sovereign debt
notes: Belgium faces one of the European Union's most acute fiscal emergencies, with a deficit of 5.2 percent of GDP and public debt approaching 108 percent in 2025. Prime Minister Bart De Wever's government is pursuing roughly ten billion euros in savings by 2029, but nationwide strikes and street protests are widening resistance to the adjustment. The standoff is becoming a test case for whether EU member states can consolidate their finances without fracturing their social contracts.
